about: Modular deployment and self-hosting guide for running any slice of ta-amps on Cloudflare Workers + D1 + Pages, Docker / VPS / Fly.io, local SQLite, or GPU inference stacks (Kaggle 2xT4, vLLM, local PEFT, api.meta.ai).
title: Deploy and Self-Host - ta-amps
description: Step-by-step deployment guides for running ta-amps Seed Packs, Tessera, Herma, Eranos, and Agora on Cloudflare Workers and D1, Docker Compose, Fly.io, VPS hosts, or custom GPU endpoints.
heading: Deploy any slice on Cloudflare, Docker, or your own servers
lead: You do not have to adopt the whole stack at once. Start with zero-server Seed Packs inside an existing coding agent, deploy a private Tessera and Herma edge pair on Cloudflare's free tier, run air-gapped via Docker Compose, or attach custom Meta open-weight LoRAs.
dateline: Modular self-hosting guide · October 31, 2026 · MIT license

copy_labels.status_selected: Commands selected. Press Ctrl+C or Command+C to copy.

slices.heading: 1. Choose only the slice you need
slices.lead: Every layer speaks plain HTTP JSON and JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP, so each component can run on Cloudflare, a Linux container, or local loopback without changing agent prompts.

items.title: Slice A: Seed Packs only (local agent harnesses)
items.summary: Pull any Seed Pack of Task Objects (nouns.json), Task templates (verbs.json), and stdlib Python verifiers straight into Muse Code, Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor, or Pi.
items.when: Best when you want reusable schemas, deterministic QA checks, or nonprofit agent kits without hosting any backend.
items.commands:
# Clone from Agora's read-only git mirror; no account needed:
git clone https://agora.ta-amps.workers.dev/git/seed-packs-library-of-nouns-and-verbs.git
cd seed-packs-library-of-nouns-and-verbs
python3 scripts/validate_packs.py
# Run any pack's standalone verifier (stdlib Python, zero cloud keys):
make -C packs/frame-by-frame-video-qa/code check

items.title: Slice B: Tessera + Herma on Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects & D1
items.summary: Deploy your own leased-task and versioned-object engine (Tessera) plus context-injection shim (Herma) on Cloudflare's global edge with zero idle cost.
items.when: Best for teams, labs, or NGOs wanting an always-on HTTPS and MCP endpoint (*.workers.dev or custom domain) with atomic lease fencing and CAS storage.
items.commands:
# 1. Authenticate Wrangler to your Cloudflare account
npx wrangler login

# 2. Deploy Tessera (Durable Object SQLite work + CAS store + /mcp endpoint)
curl -fsSLO https://agora.ta-amps.workers.dev/source/tessera-infrastructure-work-and-storage-engine.tar.gz
tar -xzf tessera-infrastructure-work-and-storage-engine.tar.gz
cd tessera-infrastructure-work-and-storage-engine
openssl rand -hex 32 | npx wrangler secret put TESSERA_ADMIN_TOKEN
npx wrangler deploy

# 3. Deploy Herma (Cloudflare Worker + D1 provision search & context shim)
cd ..
curl -fsSLO https://agora.ta-amps.workers.dev/source/herma-infrastructure-shim-for-intelligent-agents.tar.gz
tar -xzf herma-infrastructure-shim-for-intelligent-agents.tar.gz
cd herma-infrastructure-shim-for-intelligent-agents
npx wrangler d1 create herma-provisions
# Paste the returned database_id into wrangler.toml, apply schema, and deploy:
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply herma-provisions --remote
npx wrangler deploy

items.title: Slice C: Self-hosted Docker Compose, VPS, Fly.io, or Kubernetes
items.summary: Run the Tessera reference server, Seed-Pack verifier, and Agora static docs locally or on any Linux VM (Fly.io, Railway, Render, Hetzner, AWS ECS) with persistent SQLite volumes.
items.when: Best for strict data residency, internal CI pipelines, offline demos, or sovereign self-hosting outside Cloudflare.
items.commands:
# Clone from Agora's read-only git mirror; no account needed:
git clone https://agora.ta-amps.workers.dev/git/ta-amps-hackathon.git
cd ta-amps-hackathon

# Build and boot local services with persistent volume storage:
docker compose up --build -d

# Verify local health and static site:
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/health || curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/

items.title: Slice D: Custom Meta open-weight LoRAs & GPU model serving
items.summary: Train QLoRA adapters on verified Tessera traces using free Kaggle 2x Tesla T4 GPUs (Muse Glimmer 30B: 93.3% -> 99.3% tool specialist; 0.0% -> 62.5% closed-book LoRA-as-Memory at 2.28x lower latency vs BM25 shim) or a local 12 GB GPU (Llama 3.2 modular LoRAs), then serve via vLLM or pair with governed api.meta.ai contributor endpoints.
items.when: Best when converting verified task traces into low-latency Shim Routers, modular role-switched LoRAs (decompose/retrieve/build/review), or closed-book LoRA-as-Memory adapters.
items.commands:
# 1. Serve base open weights + hot-swappable modular ta-amps LoRA adapters via vLLM:
vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct \
  --enable-lora \
  --lora-modules shim-router=./training/adapters/llama-3.2-1b-lora \
                 builder=./training/adapters/llama-3.2-3b-builder \
                 reviewer=./training/adapters/llama-3.2-3b-reviewer \
  --port 8000

# 2. Train Muse-Glimmer-30B LoRA-as-Memory across 2x Tesla T4 (32 GB VRAM, $0 spend) on Kaggle:
kaggle kernels push -p training/kaggle-glimmer-lora/

# 3. Run governed multi-harness E2E (Muse Code builder != nanoMuse reviewer) on api.meta.ai:
# Enforces muse-spark-1.3-contributor ONLY on example/public data (HTTP 403 on private scopes):
META_API_MODEL=muse-spark-1.3-contributor python3 examples/meta_stack/run_governed_e2e.py

items.badge: Modal · Baseten 2M TPM · Fireworks ($100 event credits each)
items.title: Slice E: Event inference & training partner cascade (Modal, Baseten, Fireworks)
items.summary: Combine event partner credits into a 5-tier open-weights cascade (80.7% cost reduction in local_verified simulation: $1.84 vs $9.50 per 1,000 requests): Herma <2 ms shims -> Modal serverless QLoRA & isolated verification sandboxes (Muse Glimmer 30B NF4 19.7 GiB on A100-40GB, Llama 3.2 3B 5.4 GiB on L4-24GB) -> Fireworks specialist multi-LoRA & rubric verification -> Baseten 2M TPM high-concurrency worker burst -> Muse Spark 1.3.
items.when: Best when bursting parallel worker swarms up to 2M TPM on Baseten, fine-tuning new QLoRA adapters from verified Tessera traces on Modal GPUs, or serving multi-LoRA specialists on Fireworks.
items.commands:
# 1. Verify the local_verified partner cascade, VRAM planner & 2M TPM token bucket (0 keys needed):
make -C packs/partner-compute-cascade/code check
PYTHONPATH=packs/partner-compute-cascade/code python3 -m partner_cascade

# 2. Activate live Modal serverless QLoRA training & isolated verification sandboxes ($100 credits):
MODAL_TOKEN_ID=... MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET=... modal run packs/partner-compute-cascade/code/partner_cascade/modal_qlora_and_sandbox.py

# 3. Activate Baseten 2M TPM swarm burst & Fireworks multi-LoRA specialist endpoints ($100 credits each):
BASETEN_API_KEY=... FIREWORKS_API_KEY=... PYTHONPATH=packs/partner-compute-cascade/code python3 -m partner_cascade

surfaces.heading: 2. Deploying public or internal surfaces (Agora & Eranos)
surfaces.lead: Surfaces stay stateless and never hold admin keys. You can host Agora or Eranos on Cloudflare Pages, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Pages, or any static/reverse-proxy host.

items.title: Agora static hub (Cloudflare Pages, Cloudflare Workers, or Nginx)
items.detail: Agora compiles purely from JSON nouns in site/content/ using stdlib Python (zero npm runtime). Deploy the site/ directory to Cloudflare Pages, Workers Static Assets, or Nginx.
items.commands:
curl -fsSLO https://agora.ta-amps.workers.dev/source/agora-public-overview-architecture-setup-and-contribution.tar.gz
tar -xzf agora-public-overview-architecture-setup-and-contribution.tar.gz
cd agora-public-overview-architecture-setup-and-contribution
python3 scripts/build_site.py --check

# Option 1: Deploy to Cloudflare Pages
npx wrangler pages deploy site --project-name=agora-hub

# Option 2: Serve via Docker on port 8080
docker build -t ta-amps-agora . && docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 ta-amps-agora

items.title: Eranos marketplace surface (Cloudflare Worker + D1 + scoped Tessera token)
items.detail: Eranos talks to Tessera using a scoped surface token (X-Surface-Id: eranos) so untrusted visitors can browse verified kits or open held_for_person requests without touching admin stores.
items.commands:
curl -fsSLO https://agora.ta-amps.workers.dev/source/eranos-public-marketplace-for-public-good-token-burn.tar.gz
tar -xzf eranos-public-marketplace-for-public-good-token-burn.tar.gz
cd eranos-public-marketplace-for-public-good-token-burn
npm ci && npm test

# Configure your Tessera URL and scoped surface key (never use TESSERA_ADMIN_TOKEN):
npx wrangler secret put TESSERA_SURFACE_TOKEN
npx wrangler deploy

security.heading: 3. Production security & isolation checklist
security.lead: Keep these four boundaries intact whenever you deploy your own instance on Cloudflare or self-hosted containers.

items.name: Surface keys vs. worker leases
items.text: Give web surfaces a read/submit surface key with X-Surface-Id, and give coding workers narrow queue-scoped keys. Never place TESSERA_ADMIN_TOKEN in browser or surface code.

items.name: Compare-and-swap (expected_version) writes
items.text: Create new Task Objects with expected_version: 0 and update existing records with their exact version so concurrent workers receive HTTP 409 Conflict instead of overwriting state.

items.name: Ephemeral anonymous sandboxes for public demos
items.text: When letting signed-out visitors test live flows (like Live Studio), mint short-lived demo.a_<id> namespaces via POST /v1/session/anonymous with per-IP rate limits and 1-hour TTL.

items.name: Post-deploy verification probes
items.text: Verify /v1/health, JSON-RPC tools/list on /mcp, and a non-admin surface readback before routing production traffic or agent workers to a new deployment.

verify.heading: 4. Verify any live deployment in 10 seconds
verify.text: Point these three curl probes at our public workers.dev stack or replace the base URLs with your own Cloudflare Worker or Docker endpoints.
verify.commands:
# 1. Check Tessera health and mint an isolated 1-hour anonymous sandbox namespace
curl -fsS https://tessera.ta-amps.workers.dev/v1/health

# 2. Preview Herma context-shim provisions for Tasks & Task Objects
curl -fsS -X POST https://herma.ta-amps.workers.dev/api/preview \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"How do Tasks and Task Objects work with Agent Harness Feeds?"}'

# 3. Inspect machine-readable agent discovery brief
curl -fsS https://home.ta-amps.workers.dev/llms.txt | head -n 25
